transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I, um... I guess I'm here because things have gotten a bit out of hand lately. I just... I've been taking on a lot. Too much, really. More projects, signing up to teach workshops, trying to redo the studio... all while taking on extra client calls. I thought I could handle it, but... the deadlines are piling up, and the mortgage is due, and it's just... closing in on me.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless lately?
Not really, no. I wouldn't say depressed. Just... stressed out by everything I mentioned, I guess. It's just a lot to deal with.
Do you find yourself feeling overly worried or anxious about these responsibilities, even when you're not actively working on them?

I don't... I wouldn't say I'm anxious. Um. I just know what needs to get done. I don't really sit around just worrying about it when I'm away from the studio. It's just... there's a lot to do. That's all.
Have you been having thoughts or impulses that feel intrusive, unwanted, or difficult to control, even when you're trying to focus on other things?
Um, no. Not really. I mean... I think about my work, obviously, but I wouldn't call them intrusive. They're just regular thoughts. I have control over them.
Do you find it difficult to organize your tasks or stay focused on what needs to be done, even if you know it’s important?

I suppose... sometimes. It's just hard to stay on one thing. Like, I'll sit down to finish a plate for a contract, and then... I don't know, a bird at the window catches my eye, or I see a hardware catalog on the desk. Or I just get this idea for a workshop. And then I'm just... doing that instead. It just pulls me off course.

When you get distracted and switch tasks like that, does it feel like your attention is pulled away automatically, almost like a reflex, or do you feel like you're choosing to shift focus because you think something else is more important or interesting?
I don't know... it's just... I just switch. I don't really think about if it's a reflex or a choice. I just... start doing the other thing.
Do you often feel restless, as if you need to be doing something all the time, or find yourself having trouble staying still?

I guess so. Um... lately, there's just been this... humming current in me, I suppose. From the moment I wake up. I just keep moving. Rearranging the studio, drafting proposals, emailing people... fussing with my supplies. Sitting quietly just... it felt almost impossible. So I just kept doing things.
Can you think of a time when this restlessness or need to keep doing things caused you to act quickly without thinking, like making impulsive decisions or interrupting others?
I don't really know. I don't think I act without thinking. I just... do what needs to be done. I don't think I interrupt people.

Have you had trouble staying focused or organizing tasks in parts of your life outside of work, like at home or in social situations, and have these kinds of problems been happening for a long time, maybe even since you were a child?
I don't think so. I mean... I don't really remember being like that as a kid. And at home... I just do what I normally do. I don't think I have a problem organizing things. I just... live my life.
Can you recall if you had trouble staying focused or organizing tasks when you were in school, or if these kinds of problems only started more recently?
I don't think so. School was fine. I got my degree without any issues, so... I don't really remember having trouble focusing back then.

Have you ever found it hard to stay focused or felt overly active in parts of your life outside of work, like when you're at home relaxing or spending time with friends, and do you remember feeling this way even when you were younger?
I... no, not really. I mean, I just said school was fine. I don't really have trouble relaxing at home, either. I just... paint, or read. It's not hard to just sit still when I want to.

Can you think of a time when you were not at work—like when you were at home or out with friends—where you had real trouble staying focused, felt overly restless, or found yourself acting without thinking?
No... I really can't. Like I said, I'm usually just fine. I don't know why you keep asking me this. I just... I paint. I'm not restless.
Can you remember if you had any trouble focusing, staying still, or acting without thinking when you were a child, even outside of school or work settings, like at home or with friends?
I don't... I don't really know how else to say it. No. I didn't have those problems as a kid. I was just a normal child. I don't... I don't understand why we're still talking about this.
When you're at home trying to relax, like watching TV or reading, do you ever find it hard to sit still, stay focused on what you're doing, or feel like your mind is constantly racing?
I feel like I'm just repeating myself now. No. When I sit down to read, I just read. My mind isn't racing, and I sit perfectly still. I... I really don't know what else you want me to say about it.

When you're at home trying to relax or engage in leisure activities, like watching TV or reading, do you ever find it difficult to truly relax, such as feeling mentally restless or having trouble slowing your thoughts, even if you're not physically moving around?
I... I just don't. I've said this. When I want to relax, I relax. I paint, or I read, and it's fine. My thoughts are fine. I really don't have anything else to add to this.

Sometimes people feel a kind of inner tension or physical agitation that they can't seem to relieve—like feeling like you have to move, can't sit still, or even feel jittery or shaky inside. Have you ever felt something like that, even when you weren't particularly busy or stressed?
I... no. I don't get jittery. I just sit and do my work. I don't feel that inner tension you're talking about. I'm fine.

Can you describe if, during times when you are not under pressure or busy at work, you still find it difficult to focus or tend to lose track of what you're doing, even in everyday situations like following a conversation or listening to instructions?
No. I don't lose track of things. If someone is talking to me, I listen to them. My focus is... it's fine. I really don't have any issues with that.
Have you noticed any loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you usually enjoy, like painting or reading?
I still paint. I still read. It's... the same as it always is. I enjoy it fine.

Can you think of any situation, even outside of work or times when you weren't busy, where you had real trouble focusing, felt overly active, or found yourself doing things without thinking them through?
I don't... I don't really know what you mean. I just go about my day. I haven't noticed anything like that.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about everyday things, even when there isn't a clear problem or deadline causing the worry?
No, not really. I mean... I think about things, sure, but I wouldn't say I worry a lot. Just normal things. Nothing out of the ordinary.
